memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: However, if a man does not want to marry his brother's wife, she shall go to the elders at the town gate and say, "My husband's brother refuses to carry on his brother's name in Israel. He will not fulfill the duty of a brother-in-law to me." Then the elders of his town shall summon him and talk to him. If he persists in saying, "I do not want to marry her," his brother's widow shall go up to him in the presence of the elders, take off one of his sandals, spit in his face and say, "This is what is done to the man who will not build up his brother's family line." That man's line shall be known in Israel as The Family of the Unsandaled. - Deut 25:7-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
If a brother refused to fulfil this duty toward his brother's widow, there were consequences. The widow could bring the matter before the elders, and if he still refused, she would publicly remove his sandal and spit in his face, and his family would bear a name of shame. This was not primarily about cruelty, but about marking the seriousness of neglecting one's responsibility to a vulnerable family member.

The point is that refusing to care for a needy relative, when it was within his power to help, was a real failure, one that the community would not ignore. God took seriously the duty of caring for one's own family, especially the vulnerable within it. To abandon that responsibility out of selfishness was shameful.

This principle carries into the New Testament with striking force. Paul writes that anyone who does not provide for their relatives, especially their own household, has denied the faith (1 Tim 5:8). God cares deeply about how we treat our own families and those we have a responsibility toward. Caring for vulnerable relatives is not optional; it is part of living out genuine faith. This flows from the heart of God, who cares for His own family and calls us to do the same. Are there family members or others in your care whose needs God is calling you to take seriously, rather than avoiding out of self-interest?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you faithfully caring for the vulnerable in your family?
2. Where might self-interest tempt you to neglect responsibility?
3. How does God's care for His family shape yours?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me take seriously my responsibility to care for my family and those in my charge. Let me not neglect them out of selfishness. Amen.
